connections.lastfm_blurb: A free service that tracks what you listen to. Connect it to Spotify, YouTube Music, Apple Music, Navidrome and more — then Haven can show your music.
connections.lastfm_note:
First time? Sign up free at last.fm, then turn on scrobbling so it knows what you play:
• Spotify — last.fm → Settings → Applications → connect Spotify. No install.
• YouTube Music, Apple Music, Tidal — install the free Web Scrobbler browser extension.
• Navidrome, Plex, Jellyfin — enable Last.fm scrobbling in that server's own settings.
Without scrobbling set up, Haven will show nothing.
connections.lastfm_step_1: Sign in with a Last.fm account and fill in the short form (name it "Haven"; the other fields can be anything).
connections.lastfm_step_2: Copy the API key it shows you and paste it below. Ignore the shared secret — Haven does not need it.
connections.steam_step_1: Sign in with your Steam account.
connections.steam_step_2: Where it asks for a domain, any value works — Steam does not check it. Put localhost.
connections.steam_step_3: Copy the key it gives you and paste it below.
connections.spotify_blurb: Direct connection. Needs a Spotify Premium account, is harder to set up, and is limited to ~25 users. Prefer Last.fm above.
connections.spotify_step_1: Use the link above — it goes to developer.spotify.com.
connections.spotify_step_2: Sign in with your Spotify account. This needs Spotify Premium. As of 2026 the Web API is no longer available on free accounts, so the rest of these steps will not work without it (#5528). Accept the developer terms if it asks.
connections.spotify_step_3: Click Create app. You are not building software — this just registers a name. Call it "Haven".
connections.spotify_step_5: Tick Web API, save, then open Settings on the app you just made.
connections.spotify_step_6: Copy Client ID, then click View client secret and copy that too.

debug_section.title: Debug
debug_section.desc: Experimental client-side toggles. These don't change anything on the server.
debug_section.local_talk_indicator_hint: Highlight your own avatar the moment your mic crosses the talk threshold, instead of waiting for the server to echo it back. Default off — the server echo is usually preferred because it confirms your audio actually reached the server.
debug_section.mute_on_join_hint: Force the mic to start muted every time you join a voice channel. Useful if you tend to lurk first, or if you don't want to risk hot-mic'ing right after joining. You can unmute normally once you're in.
debug_section.listener_only_hint: Join voice channels without requesting microphone access. You'll hear everyone but won't be able to talk. Useful if you don't own a mic, can't grant mic permission right now, or just want to listen in. Haven will also fall back to listener-only automatically if the mic can't be opened for any reason. (#5380)
debug_section.screen_share_voice_proc: Apply voice processing to screen-share audio
debug_section.screen_share_voice_proc_hint: Re-enable echo cancellation, noise suppression, and auto gain control on the audio captured from your screen share. Default off as of 3.17.3 because these filters mangle music and game audio. Turn this on if you're sharing voice content (tutorial narration, a podcast, a meeting) where the cleanup actually helps. Does not affect your microphone, which always gets full voice processing.
debug_section.screen_audio_webaudio: Web Audio mixing for screen-share audio
debug_section.screen_audio_webaudio_hint: By default Haven plays incoming screen-share audio straight through the audio element, which keeps it in sync with the video over a TURN/relay connection. Turn this on to route it through Haven's Web Audio mixer instead, which unlocks the per-stream volume boost above 100% but can cause audio stutter and audio/video desync over a relay (it's fine on a local network). Leave it off if a screen share's audio stutters or drifts out of sync. (#5426)
debug_section.screen_relay_profile: Gentler screen share for relay connections
debug_section.screen_relay_profile_hint: Turn this on if your screen share stutters and drifts out of sync for viewers, but only when the call goes through a TURN server and never on your local network. It lowers the video bitrate back to the pre-3.18.1 values and lets the encoder drop frames when the connection is struggling, instead of holding the framerate and letting the backlog grow. Picture quality will be lower. Only the person sharing needs it on. (#5426)
debug_section.voice_glare_ice_fix: Repair voice audio after a reconnect (experimental)
debug_section.voice_glare_ice_fix_hint: If you sometimes rejoin a voice call and still can't hear one or more people until you leave and rejoin, turn this on. When two people reconnect at the same moment their connections can collide mid-repair and one direction of audio stays dead; this makes Haven re-run the repair so the audio comes back on its own. Off by default while it's still being tested. (#5444)
debug_section.disable_gpu_vsync_hint: Workaround for Nvidia G-Sync / VRR monitors where Haven Desktop drops to ~5 FPS after the window is minimized or hidden behind another window. Tells Chromium not to wait for the monitor's vsync signal before drawing frames. May cause visible tearing on monitors without variable refresh rate. Requires restart to take effect.
debug_section.unlimit_frame_rate: Remove Chromium frame-rate cap (Nvidia G-Sync fix)
debug_section.unlimit_frame_rate_hint: Pairs with the GPU vsync toggle above. Removes Chromium's internal frame-rate limit, which on some Nvidia G-Sync setups gets stuck at a very low value and never recovers. Only useful if the vsync toggle alone didn't help. Can increase CPU/GPU usage. Requires restart to take effect.

admin.admin_pw_reset_hint: ⚠️ When enabled, admins can reset any user's password to a one-time temp value. The user must change it on next login. Resetting a password also wipes that user's E2E DM history (their wrap key derives from the password). The fact that this is enabled is exposed via /api/public-config so users can see whether admins on this server have this power.
admin.oidc_desc: Let members sign in with an account from your own identity provider (Authentik, Keycloak, Authelia, Auth0 and anything else that speaks OpenID Connect) instead of a Haven password. Fill in the issuer address and client ID here, then put the client secret in your .env file as OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET and restart. The secret is deliberately kept out of the database so your backups never carry it. Register this address with your provider as the redirect URI: https://your-haven-address/api/auth/oidc/callback
admin.oidc_e2e_note: Encrypted DMs are unlocked by a key derived from what you type when you sign in, and an SSO member never types a password here. They are asked to set a separate encryption passphrase on their first sign-in, and for it again on each new device. Nobody, including you, can reset that passphrase for them.
admin.oidc_create_users_label: Create a Haven account on first sign-in
admin.oidc_create_users_hint: Off means only people who already have a Haven account linked to your provider can sign in this way. Since linking an existing account is not built yet, leaving this off will turn away everyone new.
admin.oidc_secret_warning: OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET is not set in the server environment, so the sign-in button stays hidden until it is.
admin.referrer_advanced: Advanced — use at your own discretion
admin.media_proxy_desc: Haven fetches images from other sites itself and serves them from its own cache, so your members' browsers never contact those sites. With this off, anyone who posts an image link collects the IP address and browser details of everyone who scrolls past it, without a single click. It also means embeds keep working after the original link expires or the site goes down. Costs some bandwidth and disk on your server; each image is fetched once and cached for 30 days.
admin.voice_relay_desc: Haven voice is peer-to-peer, so by default everyone in a call can see everyone else's IP address. It is how the connection is made, it needs no clicking, and nobody is told it happened. Relay-only mode routes all voice through your TURN server instead, so participants only ever see the TURN server's address. This needs a TURN server configured under Voice & Connectivity, and it uses your server's bandwidth for every call.
admin.automod_desc: Checks the links in messages, edits, DMs, profiles and channel topics against a domain policy you control. Blocked content is rejected before it is saved, so it never reaches anyone else. This matters more than it sounds: Haven renders linked images and link previews directly from the other site, so a hostile link exposes the IP address of everyone who scrolls past it, not just whoever clicks.
admin.automod_mode_hint: Allowlist is the strict option and the one that stops links you have never seen before. Blocklist only stops domains you already know about.
admin.automod_min_age: New accounts can't post links for (hours)
admin.automod_min_age_hint: 0 disables this. Applies even to allowed domains, and is the single most effective rule against register-post-link-get-banned-repeat.
admin.automod_exempt_hint: Members at or above this level are never filtered. Admins are always exempt.
admin.automod_scan_dms_hint: Direct messages are end-to-end encrypted, so the server genuinely cannot read them and cannot block a DM as it is sent. Instead the check runs in the recipient's app after it decrypts: a link to a domain you have not allowed is shown as plain text with a warning rather than something clickable, and images from those domains are not loaded. Senders are warned before the message goes out. This relies on the recipient running an app that implements it, so treat it as a strong deterrent rather than a guarantee.
admin.automod_block_ip_urls: Block links to raw IP addresses
admin.automod_preview_hint: Strongly recommended. Link previews load images straight from the other site in every viewer's browser, which hands that site everyone's IP address without a single click.
admin.automod_escalation_hint: Counts blocked attempts within a rolling window. Set any threshold to 0 to disable that step. Note that a muted member cannot send anything at all, so they stop collecting strikes until the mute runs out — if you want a fast automatic ban, set the ban threshold close to the mute threshold, or turn muting off.
admin.automod_ban_ip_hint: ⚠️ Leave off unless you understand the risk. Shared and mobile-carrier addresses mean an IP ban can catch people who did nothing.
admin.backup_hint: Download a backup of this server, or restore from a previous backup. Useful when you don't have shell access to the host machine.
admin.backup_inc_dms_hint: (E2E ciphertext; only original key holders can read)
admin.backup_modes_hint: Pick what to include. Messages and uploaded files can make the backup very large; channels / users / settings alone are usually small. User passwords, 2FA secrets, and emails are never exported.
admin.backup_restore_full_note: Only full backups can be restored here, which means the backup must have had both Messages and Uploaded files checked when it was made. Smaller channels/users/settings backups have to be re-imported by hand.
admin.backup_restore_warning: Warning: Restoring overwrites the current server data. The server will restart automatically — your hosting setup must support auto-restart (Docker, systemd, the Haven installer service, etc.). The previous database is preserved as haven.db.pre-restore for one cycle.
admin.auto_backup_hint: Auto-backups are saved to the server's data directory and pruned to your retention count. They use the same format as manual downloads, so you can restore any of them above.

admin.idle_online_desc: Lists accounts that have been connected and showing as online for hours without posting, joining voice, or changing their status. admin.referrer_policy_desc: Sets the Referrer-Policy header Haven sends to browsers, which controls how much of the current page's address is shared when the browser loads resources or follows links to other sites. The recommended options cover almost every server; the advanced policies are standard browser values left to your discretion. Policies that would send the full page address to other sites are not offered, because Haven invite links live in that address.
admin.referrer_policy_opt_default: Strict-Origin-When-Cross-Origin: within this server, shares the full address; to other sites, shares only the origin. This was Haven's default before 3.41.0 — pick it to go back to the old behaviour.
admin.referrer_policy_opt_same: Same-Origin (default): within this server, shares the full address; to other sites, shares nothing.
admin.referrer_policy_opt_none: No-Referrer: shares nothing anywhere — not even within this server.
admin.referrer_policy_note: Same-Origin and No-Referrer send nothing to other sites, so either one fixes embeds whose CDN rejects a cross-origin referrer, such as Twitter/X video. If an image or embed somewhere else stops loading after this change, that host wants a referrer: switch to Strict-Origin-When-Cross-Origin to restore the pre-3.41.0 behaviour.
admin.fcm_desc:
FCM (Firebase Cloud Messaging) is Google's system for delivering push notifications to Android phones. It's what wakes your phone when you receive a new message while Haven is closed. This means that all notifications (including your Haven username, channel name and message content) sent to your Android phone have to pass through Google's servers to reach your phone.

While this may be fine for most users, some may prefer to keep Google completely out of the equation. UnifiedPush is a decentralized notification standard that supports several notification apps, and if a UnifiedPush compatible app is installed on your phone, Haven Mobile will prioritize it over FCM.
admin.fcm_note: Dangerous Action Warning: Before disabling this, please ensure every member in your Haven server including yourself has a UnifiedPush compatible app installed on their phone. Otherwise, some members of your server will not receive any mobile notifications.

admin_reset_pw.title: Reset Password
admin_reset_pw.confirm_prompt: Generate a one-time temporary password for {username}?
admin_reset_pw.dm_warning_title: Encrypted DM history will be lost
admin_reset_pw.dm_warning_body: The user's E2E wrap key is derived from their password. Once they finish the forced change-password flow with a new password, their encrypted DM history becomes permanently unreadable on their side. The user can avoid this by signing in with their original password (which we keep on file as an escape hatch) instead of the temp one, which silently cancels this reset.
admin_reset_pw.mfa_required_body: The target user must have 2FA enabled before an admin can reset their password. Otherwise the temp password alone would be enough to take over the account. If they have not enabled 2FA, this will fail with a clear error.
admin_reset_pw.mfa_blocked_prompt: This isn't a bug. Before you can reset {username}'s password, that user needs to turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) on their own account first, under Settings → Account.
admin_reset_pw.mfa_blocked_why_body: An admin reset hands out a temporary password. If the user has no 2FA, that temp password alone would be enough for anyone who sees it (including a rogue admin) to take over the account. Requiring 2FA means the temp password is useless without their authenticator device.
